note: 091 (2026-10-29) bore record: Douglas Partners 1996 Bore 1 (Douglas Partners Working Paper No. 3 (project 24206, June 1997): piezometer completion details and test bore report, Dec 1996); surface level 176.86 m (datum unstated). Hole 14.5 m bgl: hand auger 0-4.0 m (casing to 3.5 m), rotary 4.0-14.5 m. Construction: lockable steel standpipe 0.59 m above ground; concrete well head; sand/bentonite backfill to 10.1 m; bentonite plug 10.1-10.6 m; 2-5 mm gravel pack from 10.6 m; machine-slotted screen 11.5-14.5 m; base 14.5 m. Groundwater at 3.08 m (14 Jan 1997); no free groundwater while drilling; black sheen on the drilling fluids. Lithology: sand fill to 0.7 m; sands to 3.6 m; weathered sandstone 3.6-5.9 m; fresh fine light grey sandstone with minor shale lenses from 8.9 m, 5.9-14.5 m. Unit: sandstone. In Oct-Nov 2009 the PVC was found bent and broken inside its casing (truck traffic during the cut-off wall works) and Council asked for the bore to be removed from the licence. B.MW11 (BH11, drilled Sep 2010, near Spurwood Creek) may be its replacement. Source: asset 'B.MW01 Douglas Partners 1996 Bore 1.pdf'.

091 (2026-10-29) bore record: Two bores have carried this name. (1) Results before 20 Oct 2014: Douglas Partners 1996 Bore 6 (Douglas Partners Working Paper No. 3 (project 24206, June 1997): piezometer completion details and test bore report, Dec 1996); surface level 184.21 m (datum unstated). Hole 14.5 m bgl: solid flight auger 0-4.0 m, rotary 4.0-14.5 m. Lockable steel standpipe 0.57 m above ground; sand/bentonite backfill to 11.0 m; bentonite plug 11.0-11.4 m; 1-5 mm gravel pack from 11.4 m; machine-slotted screen 11.5-14.5 m; base 14.5 m. Groundwater at 9.93 m (14 Jan 1997); no free groundwater while drilling; black sheen. Lithology: road-base fill to 0.2 m; sand to 2.0 m; weathered sandstone to 4.5 m; fresh grey sandstone with carbonaceous lenses to 14.5 m (dark grey, possibly siltstone, 10.5-12.2 m). It lay in the footprint of the bio-retention basin built by the Site Entrance Project and was replaced. (2) From 20 Oct 2014: Ground Test Pty Ltd Bore 6A (NSW Office of Water Form A and field drilling report). Depth 14.5 m bgl; 98 mm hole, solid flight auger 0-1.0 m, rotary (water) 1.0-14.5 m. PVC Class 18, 60 mm OD x 5 mm wall (50 mm ID); blank casing 0-2.0 m; machine-slotted screen 2.0-14.5 m (48 x 0.5 mm slots, horizontal); graded crushed 2-5 mm gravel pack from 1.0 m to 14.5 m (field report and sketch; the Form A table gives 2.0 m); bentonite seal 0.5-1.0 m; cuttings 0-0.5 m; lockable monument, stick-up 1.0 m at installation. No groundwater observed while drilling. Lithology: dark grey sandy soil 0-0.5 m; yellow-brown fine-grained sandstone, weathered 0.5-1.1 m and soft 1.1-3.3 m; light grey hard sandstone with some fine clayey layers 3.3-14.5 m. Unit: sandstone. Bore 6A is screened over almost its whole depth (2.0-14.5 m) where Bore 6 was screened at 11.5-14.5 m, so levels and results either side of Oct 2014 are not directly comparable. Sources: asset 'B.MW06 Douglas Partners 1996 Bore 6.pdf' (Bore 6); asset B.MW06.pdf (Bore 6A).

091 (2026-10-29) bore record: C. M. Jewell & Associates borehole log BH:11 (job J1531), drilled 9 Sep 2010 by Epoca Environmental; results start Dec 2011. Construction (scaled from the log): grout and backfill 0 to about 2.0 m; bentonite seal about 2.0-3.4 m; gravel pack from about 3.4 m to the base of the hole at about 8.4 m; screen about 3.5-6.5 m; blank sump to about 7.6 m with end cap. Unit: alluvium over sandstone; the screen spans the alluvium and the weathered sandstone below it. Council described B.MW11 to the EPA in May 2026 as a very shallow bore (about 1 m) in unconsolidated alluvium; the log does not support a 1 m depth. It stands near Spurwood Creek, as B.MW01 did, and may have replaced it. Source: asset 'B.MW11 CM Jewell 2010 BH11.pdf'.
